title: Amazon Elastic Block Store
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of amazon elastic block store and its relationship to AWS Storage Services.
Interpret the example and identify at least one prerequisite or boundary relevant to amazon elastic block store.
Propose a safe verification or troubleshooting step and record one security, reliability or cost consideration.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn amazon elastic block store in the context of AWS Storage Services. You will connect the listed subtopics to a practical decision, inspect a small example, and define evidence that would confirm or disprove your assumptions.
content.why_it_matters: Amazon Elastic Block Store matters because it is one part of aws storage services. Real workloads depend on explicit prerequisites, correct permissions, predictable behavior and a way to verify outcomes. Learning the decision points helps you distinguish a working demonstration from a safe and supportable design.

content_blocks.title: Amazon S3 protection lifecycle
content_blocks.alt_text: Objects can be uploaded, protected by access controls and encryption, versioned, transitioned using lifecycle rules, and restored or expired by policy.
content_blocks.caption: Test lifecycle rules on synthetic objects and retain data only as long as required.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text:
**Core idea.** Amazon Elastic Block Store belongs to AWS Storage Services. Select object, block and file storage by access pattern, performance, recovery and cost. For S3, preserve private defaults and configure encryption, versions, retention and lifecycle behavior deliberately.

The PDF lists these subtopics: EBS volume types; Volume attachment and resizing; EBS snapshots; Snapshot lifecycle and recovery. Treat them as a connected workflow rather than a list to memorize. Start with the workload requirement, identify the AWS resource/control involved, and write down who owns configuration and operation.

content_blocks.title: Practical reasoning
content_blocks.text: **Apply it safely.** For amazon elastic block store, name the prerequisites and the expected result before making a change. Prefer a read-only inspection or local/static example first. Then plan a normal case, a failure case, and a verification step. In a live account, require the account owner-approved sandbox, narrow permissions, spend visibility and cleanup plan. Do not put credentials in code or commit local configuration files.

items.title: EBS volume types
items.text: Identify the AWS resource or design decision involved, the permissions and prerequisites it needs, and the evidence that shows it is configured as intended.

items.title: Volume attachment and resizing
items.text: Compare the available option with the workload requirement; record the operational, security, availability and cost trade-offs rather than assuming one option is always best.

items.title: EBS snapshots
items.text: Write a verification step and a failure case. For hands-on work, start with read-only inspection and use an approved sandbox before changing cloud resources.

items.title: Snapshot lifecycle and recovery
items.text: Define the failure scenario and recovery objective, then test detection, recovery, data consistency and rollback. Treat recovery evidence as a deliverable, not an assumption.

content_blocks.title: Object protection lifecycle: Amazon Elastic Block Store
content_blocks.code: UPLOAD → PRIVATE ACCESS → ENCRYPT → VERSION → LIFECYCLE / RETENTION → RESTORE OR EXPIRE
content_blocks.expected_output: A lifecycle plan to test on synthetic objects before setting production retention.
content_blocks.run_instructions: This block is an inspectable example, not an AWS action performed by CodeLeaf. Review the example as text and adapt it only after checking current official service documentation. Do not apply/deploy changes in a real account without account-owner approval, least-privilege permissions and a reviewed cost/cleanup plan.
content_blocks.reset_steps: No AWS resource is created by this lesson example. If you independently run an approved lab, capture the starting state first, follow the lab-specific teardown instructions, check dependent resources and billing/resource inventories, and document anything retained.
content_blocks.limitations: The CodeLeaf playground is an HTML/CSS/JavaScript preview and does not execute AWS APIs, shell commands, SQL or cloud deployments. Treat output as illustrative; live values depend on credentials, permissions, Region, service state and schema.

content_blocks.title: Security and cost checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use least privilege, keep Block Public Access/private defaults unless a justified reviewed requirement says otherwise, and document cost/cleanup before live changes.

task: Create a one-page decision card for “Amazon Elastic Block Store”. State the goal, prerequisites, the AWS resource or control involved, the expected result, one read-only/static verification step, one failure case, the relevant permission boundary, and cost/cleanup considerations. Do not create or alter billable resources unless the account owner has approved the lab.
hints: Start from the exact subtopics in the lesson and define the desired state in your own words.

expected_output: A short reviewable decision card for Amazon Elastic Block Store with prerequisites, evidence, a failure case, security implications and cost/cleanup notes.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one successful example as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: The example may not test permissions, regional/service prerequisites, retries, recovery, quotas or edge cases.
common_mistakes.fix: Write acceptance criteria, test a failure path, inspect logs/state and record the limits of the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Changing a live resource before confirming its effect and cost.
common_mistakes.why: Cloud changes can expose data, break traffic or leave billable dependencies behind.
common_mistakes.fix: Start read-only, use an approved sandbox, review the change, tag ownership and verify cleanup.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying broad permissions or credentials into source files.
common_mistakes.why: Broad permissions and leaked long-lived credentials increase the impact of mistakes.
common_mistakes.fix: Use scoped roles/temporary credentials, keep secrets in approved stores and review access boundaries.

summary: Amazon Elastic Block Store is taught as part of AWS Storage Services.

Select object, block and file storage by access pattern, performance, recovery and cost. For S3, preserve private defaults and configure encryption, versions, retention and lifecycle behavior deliberately.
Verify assumptions with official service documentation and evidence from the relevant AWS resource, logs or tests.
For live labs, confirm permissions and likely charges before acting, then verify cleanup.
